rules: Any 'change' transform on $dollar_volume — TS_DELTA of the raw/LOG/TS_RANK series, or TS_CORR of TS_RANK($dollar_volume) vs its own DELAY — fails cheap_screen (|t| 0.13-0.38, 4 of 7 cheap_screen rejects this round). Use the level or TS_RANK of the level instead, which drove 4 of 6 accepts.

CS_RANK($leverage) * TS_RANK($dollar_volume, w) scored |t| 0.08 on cheap_screen, far below asset_turnover/roa/roe crossed with the same volume-rank term, which produced this round's top fitnesses. Leverage is the exception to that template, not a safe substitute.

CS_RANK($asset_turnover) * CS_RANK(-TS_MEAN($return, w)) is now saturated at w=5/10/21 (rho 0.81-0.85) even when a price-ratio term is grafted onto the return leg. Vary the fundamental or drop the return-mean leg; the window and the graft both fail to decorrelate.

Within-run duplicates (the identical expression proposed twice in one round) were this round's single biggest rejection cause: 6 of 20 (30%), more than any one screen or correlation reason. Dedupe against this round's own batch, not just the archive, before submitting.

CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($open, w)) * CS_RANK(TS_STD($open,63)/TS_STD($open,5)) shares 10 nodes across w=5 and w=10 (archive_subtree). This $open delta-times-volatility-ratio chassis is exhausted at short delta windows; the volatility-ratio leg's own windows are the untried lever.

CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($roa, 63) - $accrual_gap) is itself a saturated 6+-node fundamental block — swapping only the second multiplicative leg ($high-$low vs TS_RANK($return,5)) still collides via archive_subtree because that prefix dominates.

ABS($return) / ($dollar_volume+eps) style illiquidity ratios collapse onto plain TS_MEAN($dollar_volume) at rho 0.915. The volume denominator dominates the ratio; the return numerator adds little unless it's ranked or transformed independently first.

Multiplying ($high-$low) directly by TS_MEAN($return,5) inside a fundamental cross barely fails cheap_screen (|t| 0.98), while subtracting a separately CS_RANKed TS_MEAN($return,5) from a separately CS_RANKed product clears easily (fitness 4.834). Keep return-mean legs rank-separated, not raw-multiplied, when fusing with a range term.
